newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss industry joins Holocaust memorial fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss industry joins Holocaust memorial fund.

text.p: Swiss industry will pay 65 million Swiss francs ($44 million) into a Holocaust memorial fund launched by banks as a gesture to victims of Nazi persecution, the national industry and commerce association said on Thursday.
The industry umbrella group said its membership had pledged the money but declined to say which sectors or which companies would pay how much and which ones would not participate.

"At the initiative of the Swiss Commerce and Industry Association, numerous companies from leading Swiss business sectors have declared their willingness to join in rapid humanitarian aid for needy Holocaust survivors," the group said in a statement.
The industry payment would bring the fund to 265 million Swiss francs.

Galvanised by international pressure and threats of losing business, big Swiss banks last month contributed 100 million Swiss francs to start the fund, which is being coordinated by the Swiss government and world Jewish groups.
Then the government this week said the central bank would also pay 100 million Swiss francs.

Each party to the fund has had different grounds for paying. The commercial banks were trying to dispel claims that they hoarded accounts left by Holocaust victims while the national bank was making amends for buying looted Nazi gold during World War Two.

Swiss machine makers and engineering industries, who are part of the industry and commerce association, last week spoke out in favour of donating to the Holocaust fund in order to repair the tarnished image of Swiss business.

Some Swiss industrialists have been accused of helping the German war effort or of profiting from Nazi crimes by using forced labour at plants in Germany or buying businesses cheaply after they were stolen from Jewish owners.
